text:
erika: quick heads-up — I ran a multi-GPU perf sweep this morning for KV-cache sharding strategies. compared tile-by-seq (time-tiling), shard-by-layer (layer sharding), and full-replication across TP/PP/DP mixes. attaching a short profiling snapshot below and a few surprising regressions.

erika: hardware: 8x A100-80GB NVLINK per node, model: gpt-like 30B, sequence lengths: 256/1024/2048, microbatch: 1/4/8. runs include TP-only (8-way TP), PP-heavy (2 stages, pipeline microbatching), and DP x2.

erika: profiling excerpt (condensed):
```
[profile] config: {kv_strategy: tile-by-seq, TP:8, PP:1, DP:1, overlap_comm: true, async_allreduce: true}
[time] total_tokens: 1.2M, tokens/sec: 42k, avg_latency_ms: 28, p99_ms: 84
[kernel] qk_matmul: optimized_fused_attention (fast path)
[comm] all-reduce: async(grad), overlap_ratio: 0.46, all-reduce-ms: 2.8
[kv] kv_shard_copy: 4.3ms per step, kv_lookup: 1.1ms
```

tom: nice. what's the baseline (replication) numbers for the same config?

erika: replication baseline (same run): tokens/sec: 35k, avg_latency_ms: 34, p99_ms: 92. replication reduces cross-GPU comm but increases memory and per-token GPU compute because each GPU stores full KV -> worse throughput here.

sasha: did you toggle NCCL async/allreduce overlap? last month we saw blocking all-reduce on the FP16 reduction path cause p99 spikes.

erika: yes — these runs had overlap enabled. interestingly, with TP-heavy setups overlap helps tile-by-seq significantly (reduces idle compute during KV sync). with PP-heavy pipelines, overlap helps less because pipeline bubbles dominate microbatch scheduling.

luis: how about shard-by-layer? I remember it reduces KV duplication but introduces cross-stage fetches. memory and comm tradeoffs?

erika: shard-by-layer: memory down ~12% vs replicate, tokens/sec ~40k (between tile & replicate). but we observed extra NCCL all-to-all for KV fetches across layer shards: all-to-all-ms: 6.2, overlap_ratio: 0.28. this hits harder at long seq (2048) where per-step KV volume is larger.

anya: any sign of the perf regression we saw in canary-2 yesterday? someone mentioned p99 regressions when kernel selection fell back.

erika: yes — on one canary run I saw ~8% worse p99 for tile-by-seq. traced to kernel-selection fallback: attention kernel chose generic matmul path for certain seq+kv tile sizes after the compiler changed heuristics. log snippet:
```
[warn] kernel_selector: preferred=optimized_fused_attention, selected=matmul_generic, reason=tile_match_fail (seq=1536, kv_tile=64)
[trace] qk_matmul_gemm: time 3.9ms -> 6.7ms (fallback)
```

erika: that fallback explains the p99 bump. it's a conservative selection when workspace < threshold; we should tune workspace heuristic or add a quick fallback to force the fused kernel when kv_shard_strategy==tile-by-seq and TP>4.

tom: return-on-effort question: is it worth adding a dynamic heuristic that picks shard strategy at runtime based on TP/PP/seq? or better to keep config-time selection and surface recommendation in Redwood Optimize?

sasha: my vote: implement a small runtime heuristic plus an Optimize suggestion. heuristics: if TP>=4 and seq>=1024 prefer tile-by-seq; if PP>1 and microbatch<=2 prefer shard-by-layer; if low memory (device_free < 60%) prefer replicate for latency-sensitive single-request workloads.

luis: also consider all-reduce size thresholds: when KV shard messages exceed X MB, prefer shard-by-layer to avoid huge NCCL all-reduces. we should measure break-even point.

erika: agreed. next steps I'm taking:
- open a perf PR to tune kernel-selector thresholds for fused attention (prevent that matmul fallback for common kv_tile sizes).
- add a lightweight runtime heuristic in the serving runtime that suggests/forces kv_shard_strategy based on TP/PP/seq/microbatch.
- instrument more detailed per-step all-reduce breakdown (separate KV vs grad) so we can set the MB threshold luis mentioned.

perf-bot: job #perf-sweep-2026-03-18 completed: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/kv-sweep/1768501234/ (contains raw nvprof traces + flamegraphs). :white_check_mark:

anya: thanks erika — can you drop the PR link here when ready? i'll try the heuristic against a couple internal-prod models. :thumbsup:

erika: will do. will also add a short note to the eng-runtime README about expected tradeoffs (tile-by-seq best for TP-dominant long-seq; shard-by-layer best when PP and microbatching is heavy; replicate for lowest tail and simpler scheduling).

luis: if anyone wants the raw nvprof slices ping me, i'll upload a compressed sample for 2048 seq tile-by-seq.

erika: thanks all — I'll track in GH issue #INF-1892 and follow up with numbers and a tiny canary to ensure no regressions on kernel selection.
